sources.limits: Readable official page directly identifies the Nueltin area with the Thlewiaza River system and Hudson Bay drainage through Nunavut. This is system-level context, not a complete line-by-line name assignment or evidence for the model's northern attachment.

sources.limits: Readable original official map inspected. Supports Nueltin geometry and the named Thlewiaza outlet/eastward corridor. Historical topographic base and thematic overlays are not a current channel survey or evidence that lake passages have river names.

sources.title: Edehon Lake, 65A, Land Use Information Series, 1:250,000
sources.author: Canada, Department of the Environment; Indian and Northern Affairs; Agriculture Canada thematic cartography

sources.limits: Original sheet, readable corridor details, graticules, name labels and imprint inspected. Distinguishes the northern Tha-anne and southern Thlewiaza corridors. It does not establish the selected modeled southward connector as one named natural river. Base information is stated as current to 1961; thematic map was produced in 1979. No claim of present-day connectivity or exact divide coordinates is made.

sources.title: Henik Lakes, 65H, Land Use Information Series, 1:250,000

sources.title: Creel census and biological investigation of North Henik, South Henik, Nueltin and Snowbird lakes, Northwest Territories
sources.author: M. M. Roberge, L. Dahlke and C. J. Read; Department of Fisheries and Oceans
sources.page: Canadian Data Report of Fisheries and Aquatic Sciences 469, printed page 1, PDF page 9
sources.limits: Readable original-PDF web text inspected for the study-area drainage descriptions. Nueltin is assigned to Thlewiaza, North Henik to Tha-Anne, and South Henik to McConnell–Tha-anne–Kognak. Historical regional descriptions corroborate separation; the report was not used to locate the exact modeled connector or as a current hydrological survey. No map from this report was relied upon.

sources.title: Geological map of Greenland 1:2 500 000

correspondence.finding: The actual selected mainstem and northern attachment were inspected as complete paths and by their geographic turns against readable official map graticules, water shapes, river labels and neighboring corridors. The comparison included the western southward loop, the long northeast passage through Nueltin, the outlet turn east, the Edehon and Ranger Seal lake passages, the coastal termination, and the northern branch's separate lake chain and southward modeled connection. Neither the collection bounding box nor MAIN_RIV was treated as a name assignment.

The Manitoba geological map places the western modeled route in the Snyder–Kasmere lake-chain setting, followed by the east/northeast approach to Nueltin Lake. It distinguishes neighboring Cochrane drainage to the southwest and Putahow drainage farther north/east. The short westernmost extension lies west of the Manitoba sheet boundary; its local channel name is unresolved, and no Snyder, Kasmere or Thlewiaza name is assigned to that extension solely from its modeled continuation. The provincial park description independently identifies the Nueltin drainage as the Thlewiaza River system.

Sheet 65B directly matches the selected southwest-to-northeast lake passage along Nueltin's elongated main body and the northern outlet turning east into the channel labeled Thlewiaza River. Nueltin's side bays and other inflows are separately visible; lake passages are retained as lake passages rather than relabeled as river reaches. The modeled northernmost mainstem bend is at the Nueltin outlet corridor, not at the independently mapped Henik lakes farther north.

Sheet 65A follows the named Thlewiaza east from the Nueltin sheet, then southeast through Edehon Lake and northeast out of its eastern side. The actual modeled mainstem has the same sequence of turns and lake setting. The sheet separately prints Tha-anne River along its northern edge; that is a distinct mapped corridor, not an alternative label for the Thlewiaza channel.

Sheet 55D matches the continuation through the Ranger Seal Lake setting, the east/northeast lower Thlewiaza course and its Hudson Bay outlet. Its readable Thlewiaza labels, lake form, coastal position and river bends support the lower mainstem identity. The map also depicts the neighboring Tha-anne/McConnell-side coastal drainage farther north, preventing a nearest-label transfer between the separate routes.

The northern piece follows the Gregoire/Boland and Hicks–Elliott lake-chain setting on sheet 65G, then turns east along the Kognak corridor through the Griffin/Ducker-side country. Sheet 65H directly labels Kognak River on the corresponding approach south of the Henik lakes and shows its eastern junction in the Tha-anne/Roseblade Lake setting. These are supported northern-corridor names; they are not aliases of Thlewiaza and are not applied indiscriminately to every intervening lake passage.

At the 65H–65A sheet boundary, the northern modeled continuation meets the mapped Tha-anne corridor. The selected 2721 piece then bends south and southwest through the intervening lake/stream terrain toward the Hopton–Downer lake setting and finally the Thlewiaza east of Edehon. The readable mapping shows Tha-anne continuing east and does not establish the model's whole southward transition as a named, connected through-river. Printed lake levels also caution against interpreting this modeled sequence as a verified downstream connection. This is a geographical connectivity/name-scope concern, not a claim that a modern hydrological survey has proved every possible intermittent connection absent.

The DFO report independently calls Nueltin part of the Thlewiaza system while placing North Henik in the Tha-Anne system and South Henik in a McConnell–Tha-anne–Kognak system. This distinction agrees with the map labels and reinforces why the northern modeled attachment cannot automatically inherit the principal Thlewiaza identity. It does not itself locate the exact model-divide crossing or authorize modifying the geometry.

The selected eastern end first turns north and then west south of Aceguá, before joining the Negro corridor and turning southwest. The MGAP Cerro Largo sheet's graticule, mapped drainage and town/department configuration distinguish this feeder from the Negro arriving from the north. Its local name is left unassigned. The selected route therefore does not represent the complete named river from its Brazilian source.

After that feeder junction, the selected course follows the Negro's southwestern departmental-boundary corridor and then its predominantly westward reach. The north-side Tacuarembó junction and subsequent bend toward the upper Rincón del Bonete setting correspond on the Cerro Largo and Tacuarembó sheets and DINACEA basin maps. No exact name-transition vertex is inferred from the model's fragment boundaries.

The long downstream piece continues through the Rincón del Bonete reservoir setting toward Paso de los Toros, then the Baygorria and Palmar succession and lower Río Negro. The MGAP Tacuarembó and Río Negro sheets show the reservoir outlines, outlet corridors and successive bends. DINACEA explicitly treats these as three reservoirs on the middle river. A generalized model line across an impoundment is not a separately named natural channel.

West of Palmar, the route follows the winding lower corridor past the Mercedes setting and toward Villa Soriano and the Río Uruguay outlet. The Río Negro departmental sheet supplies graticule and the distinctive southward and southwestward lower bends. Its islanded mouth context supports the system endpoint but does not assign a local distributary name to the model's simplified final segment.

The northern chain approaches from the Rivera border vicinity, runs south in the Cuñapirú corridor, then continues in the Tacuarembó corridor toward the Negro. DINACEA Figure 40 separates Cuñapirú from Tacuarembó Grande and Tacuarembó Chico. The 2024 monitoring report independently places Cuñapirú stations in Rivera and at Paso Cunha, and Tacuarembó stations at Villa Ansina and farther south. The short initial feeder pieces and exact confluence vertices remain unnamed; the whole northern chain is not called Negro or uniformly Tacuarembó.

The southern chain follows the westward Yí corridor, including its broad southern sweep and northwestward lower approach to Negro/Palmar. DINACEA Figure 64 shows the same corridor with Sarandí del Yí and Durazno context, while Figures 1–2 and the direct description distinguish Yí as the southern tributary. The selected eastern tip is not asserted to be the Yí's natural source, and no local feeder or reservoir-entry boundary is assigned.

correspondence: The complete actual cached fragment 13894 was inspected, including the northern starting leg, western southward course, broad southern turn, eastward middle course, northward Itambé bend, southeastward lower course and coastal termination. Readable graticules, channel shapes, junctions and settlement relationships were used; the bounding box and MAIN_RIV membership were not substituted for full-route correspondence.

The initial modeled north–south leg lies in the Santo Antônio do Retiro–Montezuma headwater setting and turns east toward the south-flowing Pardo corridor. IBGE’s Santo Antônio do Retiro sheet supplies readable stream and municipal-boundary context for this entire approach. ANA’s Article 1 specifies a Pardo source farther east. The selected starting vertex therefore cannot be called that official source point, and an individual name for the complete initial approach is left unassigned.

The following southward reach corresponds to the corridor explicitly labeled Rio Pardo on IBGE’s Rio Pardo de Minas sheet, including its approach to the municipal seat and subsequent southeastward turn. The sheet distinguishes adjacent streams. Their labels and the names of nearby settlements are not transferred to the selected starting branch.

ANA’s original Annex I provides the connecting upper-to-middle basin sequence: the southern bend below Rio Pardo de Minas, Passagem das Éguas control vicinity, eastward approach through the Machado Mineiro reservoir corridor, and continuation toward Cândido Sales and Encruzilhada. Article 1 separately describes the upper and middle Pardo reaches. This supports system continuity without renaming the reservoir or treating a modeled reservoir centerline as proof of a separate river name or present operating flow.

INEMA’s 2014 original map follows the entire Bahian course from the Minas Gerais border. Its labeled Pardo runs past Cândido Sales, bends north toward Itambé, turns east and then southeast toward Potiraguá, and continues through the Mascote corridor. This distinctive sequence matches the selected line. The Catolé Grande approach from Itapetinga is separately drawn and is not substituted for the Pardo main course.

The 2010 official monitoring report independently names successive Pardo sampling reaches near Cândido Sales/Encruzilhada, Ribeirão do Largo, the Potiraguá approach, Pau Brasil, Mascote and Canavieiras. Its original basin map and unifilar diagram distinguish the Pardo sequence from monitored tributaries. These geographically ordered points reinforce the visual middle-to-lower correspondence; historical water-quality results are not treated as present conditions.

The eastern end follows the Pardo corridor from Mascote toward Canavieiras on SEI’s detailed municipal sheet. The sheet separately draws the coastal channels and the Jequitinhonha farther south. The modeled terminal point is a generalized Canavieiras coastal ending, not an exact assignment of every estuarine branch or contemporary mouth position. No coastal-channel or neighboring-river name is applied to the full group.

correspondence.object_scope: The single cached mainstem fragment was inspected over its complete displayed route, including the far-eastern northward hook, the long westward run with central bends and the final southward western leg. No other tributary fragment is present in the cached group.
correspondence.displayed_length_limit: Model display length only, not an independently established length of a natural river.
correspondence.full_path_finding: The eastern hook and long middle section are in the mapped Inland Ice interior. The westward line gradually approaches the western ice margin, then turns south in the broad sector between the Upernavik Isfjord and Rink Isbræ/Karrat Isfjord contexts. The actual path was read against the source graticule and ice/land pattern; the regional bounding box alone was not used to assign an identity.
correspondence.name_limit: The source does not show the complete modeled line as one named surface river, subglacial river or glacier. Names of nearby glaciers, fjords and settlements do not provide a river name for the long interior path. The exact marginal outlet identity remains unassigned.
correspondence.map_interpretation: Surface contours, dashed ice-thickness isopachs and sub-ice bedrock contours describe ice and terrain rather than named river courses. Neither the model route nor this map establishes actual hydrological connectivity, present flow or permanence.
correspondence.historical_scope: The 1995 mapped ice edge and the 2009 explanatory text are historical feature-class context; no current margin, melt rate or discharge is inferred.
correspondence.conclusion: Readable full-route regional coverage is sufficient for a completed naming scope hold, with null names and automatic application disabled.

scope_limit: MAIN_RIV groups and model mainstem roles do not establish a uniform name for every included reach, tributary or lake passage. Source observations support only the stated representative identity or hold.
publication_boundary: Own factual observations, attribution and official public URLs only; source originals, images, complete coordinates and private evidence remain omitted.
